items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: My style's been influenced, it's a bit too much like George Lewis I suppose at present

ctx.x: And this is in the forties mostly you're talking about?

Um, into the fifties too. Um. Um. No one, uh, took, uh, any great heed of the, um, Bunk Johnson, George Lewis, uh, type of band when it came out, um, until, um, 1957 when the Melbourne New Orleans Band, uh, started. Um. Um. They stayed very much in the old, uh, mold of, uh, King Oliver Lou Bottas, sort of thing.
Well, uh, back to Frank Johnson. Who was the star of that band? Was Johnson himself a star? I know.

items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: INTERVIEWER: You're not going to play this to George I hope. [INTERVIEWEE] No, no. I regard him as an amateur...

ctx.x: Yes, in jazz. Because he's not a clever player. He's not... Is this going over? Yeah, go ahead.
You're not a showman. You're trapped. You're not going to play this to George I hope.

No, no. I regard him as an amateur and his... That's why he's... That's why he's good. Yes. That's why also he's made a lot of records where he's out of tune and having a lot of trouble. There is one I just couldn't play it. It was so far... He was sort of... He was playing quite a good intonation himself, but he was out of tune with everyone else in the band so much that they just... He was in tune with himself, but not with anybody else.
